html:
SMTO-EXE-0025 — A command failed without saying why

GUID: 5c159ef7-ee9f-44ad-a24a-00dc629916a9
Slug: execution-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • A step in your task reported that it failed, but it gave no clear reason. It may have done part of its work before it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the failed step in the task and read its output, especially the last few lines, for a message from the command itself. The command's own output often names the real problem, such as a missing file or a refused password.
  2. Check the thing the step was working on, such as the file, folder or service. Or ask SMTO in the conversation to look at it without changing anything. The step may have finished part of its work before it failed, and running it again could repeat that part.
  3. Only if nothing was changed, fix the problem the output names, then ask SMTO to do the step again. Repeating the step is safe only once you know the first attempt left nothing half done.

What success looks like

  • The step shows as completed and its output shows the result you expected.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Then select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking SMTO to repeat the step; each attempt may change something again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The execution result reports a failure (Gateway failed/error status, stream error, nonzero Python wrapper exit or empty error text) without a more specific error kind.

What this means

  • Execution supplied a failed status or stream error without a narrower category, or the output layer needed a fallback for an empty error. A nonzero exit is one producer, not a complete cause for this category. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Execution supplied a failed status or stream error without a narrower category, or the output layer needed a fallback for an empty error. A nonzero exit is one producer, not a complete cause for this category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact exit status, process state, stderr and execution/effect facts; do not infer timeout or no effects from an exit number alone.

How to fix it

  • Read the step's stderr, exit_code, process_state and error_kind in the operation receipt (ShellExecutor._result / gateway_core.process_outcome.completion_facts) and the Gateway job record. Establish on the target what the command actually changed before authorizing a corrected command; do not replay it blindly.
  • Inspect the bounded execution receipt and specific failure detail. Reconcile partial or uncertain effects before correcting or repeating work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original outcome and any partial effects are understood before a corrected operation is authorized.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
